subject: spanish
promptStrong: Give me a challenging AQA GCSE Spanish (8692) exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the spec and show the ideal response.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for AQA GCSE Spanish (8692) simply, with clear examples and the most common mistake, then give me 5 quick practice items to try.

questions.q: Describing your family, which sentence has every adjective agreeing correctly?
options: Mi madre es alto y delgado.
Mi padre es baja y rubio.
Mis hermanas son simpáticas y trabajadoras.
Mis primos son inteligente y divertido.
questions.explain: Adjectives agree in gender AND number with the noun. 'Mis hermanas' is feminine plural, so the adjectives take -as: simpáticas, trabajadoras.

questions.q: Complete: «Mi hermano ___ mucho deporte.» (from hacer — he does)
questions.explain: hacer is irregular only in the 'yo' form (hago); the rest are regular, so él/ella → hace.

questions.q: What is the correct 'yo' (I) form of dormir (to sleep)?
questions.explain: dormir is an o→ue 'boot' verb: (yo) duermo. Only nosotros/vosotros keep the plain stem (dormimos, dormís).

questions.q: Choose the right verb: «Mi mejor amiga ___ muy cansada hoy.» (very tired today)
questions.explain: Tiredness is a temporary state, so it takes estar: 'está cansada'. Using ser would wrongly make it a permanent trait.

questions.q: Daily routine: «Todos los días (yo) ___ a las siete.» (I get up)
questions.explain: levantarse is reflexive, so the 'yo' form keeps its reflexive pronoun: me levanto.

questions.q: Complete: «Me ___ las asignaturas de ciencias.» (I like science subjects)
questions.explain: gustar agrees with the thing liked, not the person. 'las asignaturas' is plural, so it must be gustan.

questions.q: How do you say 'I am going to study medicine'?
questions.explain: The near future is ir a + infinitive: 'Voy a estudiar'. The 'a' is essential — 'voy estudiar' is incorrect.

questions.q: «El fin de semana pasado (yo) ___ al gimnasio.» (I went — last weekend)
questions.explain: A completed action at a specific past time needs the preterite. ir and ser share it: (yo) fui. 'iba' (imperfect) would mean 'used to go'.

questions.q: Higher tier — «Cuando ___ mayor, quiero estudiar medicina.» (when I'm older)
questions.explain: After 'cuando' pointing to the future, Spanish uses the present subjunctive: 'cuando sea mayor'. This is a Higher-tier structure (Cluster 9).

questions.q: What does «llevarse bien con alguien» mean?
options: to get on well with someone
questions.explain: 'llevarse bien con' = to get on well with. Its opposite is 'llevarse mal con' (to get on badly with).

questions.q: A friend is described as «testarudo». They are…
questions.explain: 'testarudo/a' = stubborn — a common personality adjective for Theme 1 descriptions.
'hijo único' / 'hija única' = only child. 'hijo mayor' = eldest child, 'gemelo' = twin, 'sobrino' = nephew.
'llevar una vida sana' = to lead a healthy life ('sano/a' = healthy).

questions.q: Which of these is a healthy habit («un hábito sano»)?
questions.explain: 'evitar el estrés' = to avoid stress (healthy). 'fumar' = to smoke, 'comida basura' = junk food — both unhealthy.
'el bienestar' = wellbeing, linked to 'sentirse bien' (to feel well).
'aprobar' = to pass; 'suspender' = to fail. A classic false friend — 'aprobar' does not mean 'approve' here.
